intent: Baseline geometry with 5 evenly spaced sensors of moderate size, balanced body and wheel dimensions, and moderate mass to provide stable, responsive line following. Expect good line detection and stable control as a foundation for integration feedback.
rationale: Starting from scratch with no prior geometry or integration feedback, I propose a balanced, conservative sensor and body layout to maximize line detection and stable control. I choose 5 sensors spaced evenly across the front, covering left to right, to detect the tape line effectively, with a moderate sensor size of 0.012 m to balance resolution and coverage. The wheel track is set to 0.12 m, a middle value for stability and maneuverability, with a wheel radius of 0.03 m for moderate speed and torque. The body width is 0.12 m, matching the wheel track for compactness and off-track tolerance, and the body length is 0.18 m to provide enough space for components without excessive size. Mass is set to 0.8 kg, a moderate value to balance inertia and agility. The intent is to provide a solid baseline geometry that the integrator can build a controller on, expecting reasonable line detection and stable driving. Hypotheses include that 5 sensors with moderate size will detect the line well without excessive noise, and that the chosen dimensions will allow stable, responsive driving. I request measurements of completion, progress, line_loss_events, rms_error, and max_error to evaluate line following success, stability, and off-track events.
